brief: GS Research's August core PCE print rose 0.25% m/m, below expectations, with the y/y rate at 3.01%, also below expectations; a downward methodology-driven revision, mostly from the portfolio management component, was larger than GS expected. GS lowers its Q4/Q4 core PCE forecast to 3.0%, below the FOMC median of 3.4%. Combined with NY Fed President Williams' comments, GS now sees an October hike as unlikely, pushes the second hike to December, and sees a strong chance the FOMC ultimately judges further hikes unnecessary. Separately, yields still rose on the day as the street looked through the soft print. In equities: GS upgrades OXY (PT $69) on debt reduction, a $4.0bn self-help cash-flow target by 2030 and valuation, and downgrades TOU to Sell (PT C$49) on Western Canadian gas weakness and valuation. GS expects Micron shares modestly higher post-print on guidance ahead of Street despite gross-margin softness, keeping its Neutral rating. DoorDash's Dash Forward event signals continued evolution toward three-sided local commerce. Quarter-end flows show an $11.5B MOC sell imbalance, pension selling at the 89th percentile, short-interest unwind, and a Software-over-Semis tilt into Micron's print.
